title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Mock Exam #19

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #19
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A student puts a plant in a box with a small hole on one side. After a week, the plant bends toward the hole. This shows that plants (1 mark)
   A. need no water
   B. make sound
   C. walk
   D. respond to light

2. Which of these do plants need to stay alive? (1 mark)
   A. Only sand
   B. Stones and plastic
   C. Water, air and light
   D. Only darkness

3. Which sign of life do ALL living things eventually show? (1 mark)
   A. Flying
   B. Dying
   C. Flowering
   D. Making seeds

4. Which of these is NOT an animal? (1 mark)
   A. A housefly
   B. A wooden toy horse
   C. A cow
   D. A tilapia

5. Which of these is an insect? (1 mark)
   A. Butterfly
   B. Earthworm
   C. Snail
   D. Crab

6. Why should you limit sweets and sugary drinks? (1 mark)
   A. They cause tooth decay
   B. They make you taller
   C. They help digestion
   D. They make teeth stronger

7. Which part of the digestive system is long and coiled? (1 mark)
   A. Mouth
   B. Gullet
   C. Rectum
   D. Small intestine

8. Which of these is a good use of a school deworming day? (1 mark)
   A. Throw them away
   B. Refuse to take them
   C. Take the tablets when given by the health worker
   D. Give them to animals

9. What is saliva? (1 mark)
   A. A liquid in the mouth that wets food
   B. A type of waste
   C. A tube in the stomach
   D. A germ

10. Why is a plan for a healthy digestive system useful? (1 mark)
   A. It makes us grow overnight
   B. It reminds us to do the right things every day
   C. It stops us feeling hungry
   D. It cures all diseases at once

11. Which of these is a liquid? (1 mark)
   A. Sugar
   B. Chalk
   C. Cooking oil
   D. Air in a football

12. Which is an example of reducing waste? (1 mark)
   A. Leaving litter at a picnic
   B. Carrying a cloth shopping bag
   C. Throwing a bottle in a river
   D. Burning plastic

13. A wrapper of biscuits is made of plastic. Which type of waste is it? (1 mark)
   A. Non-decomposable
   B. Liquid
   C. Decomposable
   D. Gas

14. What should you do if you find a needle or broken glass in waste? (1 mark)
   A. Pick it up with bare hands
   B. Put it in your pocket
   C. Tell a teacher and do not touch it
   D. Play with it

15. Why is burning plastic bad? (1 mark)
   A. It makes harmful smoke
   B. It makes good manure
   C. It is safe for everyone
   D. It makes rain

16. Why should we not throw waste in rivers? (1 mark)
   A. It pollutes the water
   B. It helps fish
   C. It makes water sweet
   D. It makes water clean

17. Which of these is an example of a place where water may be recycled? (1 mark)
   A. A water treatment plant
   B. A tap
   C. A road
   D. A dry shamba

18. A dripping tap fills a 5 litre bucket in one day. How much water is wasted in 4 days? (1 mark)
   A. 1 litre
   B. 54 litres
   C. 9 litres
   D. 20 litres

19. Which of these is true of water? (1 mark)
   A. Only humans need water
   B. Animals do not need water
   C. Water is needed by all living things
   D. Plants do not need water

20. Why does a mango fall from a tree? (1 mark)
   A. Friction pushes it
   B. Sound moves it
   C. Light pulls it
   D. Gravity pulls it down

21. A wheelbarrow is easier to move than dragging a load because (1 mark)
   A. Gravity is less
   B. The wheel reduces friction
   C. The wheel is heavy
   D. The load gets smaller

22. Which of these reduces friction? (1 mark)
   A. Rough paint
   B. Sand on a surface
   C. Gluing parts
   D. Ball bearings

23. Which of these only reflects light? (1 mark)
   A. A candle
   B. A torch
   C. A firefly
   D. The moon

24. Which of these could you use to test three cards for straight line travel of light? (1 mark)
   A. A ruler only
   B. A cup of water
   C. Cards with holes in the middle and a torch
   D. A bell

25. What is a transparent material? (1 mark)
   A. A material that lets almost all light pass through
   B. A material that is always red
   C. A material that makes light
   D. A material that blocks all light

26. Which of these is a safety rule about the sun? (1 mark)
   A. Shine a mirror in eyes
   B. Go out at midday without shade
   C. Never look directly at it
   D. Look at it for a long time

27. Where should children be when an adult is cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Holding the pot
   B. Next to the fire
   C. On top of the cooker
   D. Away from the fire

28. What is evaporation? (1 mark)
   A. Water being poured
   B. Liquid water turning into a gas
   C. Water becoming a solid
   D. Water freezing

29. Which use of heat helps farmers to store maize? (1 mark)
   A. Making shadows
   B. Colouring paper
   C. Drying grain
   D. Writing

30. Why should electric irons be unplugged after use? (1 mark)
   A. To make them hot
   B. To make them noisy
   C. To make them heavier
   D. To prevent burns and fire

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain why a spider is not an insect. (3 marks)

32. Explain why friction can be both useful and a problem. Give two examples of each. (4 marks)

33. Explain how animals show the signs of life: feeding, growing, and reproducing. Give an example of each. (4 marks)

34. Describe how you can care for plants at school and at home. Give five ways. (5 marks)

35. A pupil says that empty containers have nothing inside. Explain why the pupil is wrong and how you would show it. (5 marks)

36. Give three examples of how plants respond to changes around them. (3 marks)

37. Give two examples each of vertebrates and invertebrates, and state one feature of each group. (4 marks)

38. Explain how wet clothes dry in the sun. (3 marks)

39. Describe how you would show that air takes up space using a cup, tissue paper and a basin of water. (4 marks)

40. Describe how heat is used in cooking and warming in a home. (4 marks)

41. Give three safety measures during waste management. (3 marks)

42. Explain the dangers of diarrhoea and what should be done to help someone who has it. (5 marks)

43. Explain why sand is not a liquid although it can be poured. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #19 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — respond to light
   The plant responds to the light entering through the hole.

2. C — Water, air and light
   Plants need water, air, light and nutrients from the soil.

3. B — Dying
   Every living thing dies one day, but not all fly, flower or make seeds.

4. B — A wooden toy horse
   A toy is not alive. It does not feed, grow or reproduce.

5. A — Butterfly
   A butterfly has six legs and three body parts.

6. A — They cause tooth decay
   Sugar feeds germs that damage teeth.

7. D — Small intestine
   The small intestine is a very long coiled tube.

8. C — Take the tablets when given by the health worker
   Follow the health worker's advice.

9. A — A liquid in the mouth that wets food
   Saliva wets food and starts to digest starchy foods.

10. B — It reminds us to do the right things every day
   A plan helps us follow healthy habits.

11. C — Cooking oil
   Cooking oil flows and takes the shape of its container.

12. B — Carrying a cloth shopping bag
   A reusable bag means fewer plastic bags are thrown away.

13. A — Non-decomposable
   Plastic wrappers do not rot easily.

14. C — Tell a teacher and do not touch it
   Sharp objects should be handled by adults using tools.

15. A — It makes harmful smoke
   Burning plastic gives off harmful smoke.

16. A — It pollutes the water
   Waste makes water dirty and unsafe.

17. A — A water treatment plant
   Treatment plants clean used water.

18. D — 20 litres
   5 x 4 = 20 litres.

19. C — Water is needed by all living things
   All living things need water.

20. D — Gravity pulls it down
   Gravity acts on every object.

21. B — The wheel reduces friction
   Wheels roll and reduce friction.

22. D — Ball bearings
   Ball bearings roll and reduce friction.

23. D — The moon
   The moon reflects sunlight.

24. C — Cards with holes in the middle and a torch
   Aligned holes let light pass only when straight.

25. A — A material that lets almost all light pass through
   Transparent materials let us see clearly through them.

26. C — Never look directly at it
   The sun can harm eyes.

27. D — Away from the fire
   Children stay away from the cooker.

28. B — Liquid water turning into a gas
   Evaporation changes a liquid into a gas.

29. C — Drying grain
   Heat dries wet things.

30. D — To prevent burns and fire
   Switching off prevents accidents.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Insects have six legs and three body parts. A spider has eight legs, so it is not an insect. It is an invertebrate.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for six legs, 1 mark for eight legs, 1 mark for conclusion.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Useful: brakes stop bicycles and shoes grip the ground. A problem: it wears out tyres and makes machines hot.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying it helps in some cases and harms in others, and 1 mark for each correct example up to 3.

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: Feeding: a goat eats grass. Growing: a chick becomes a hen. Reproducing: a hen lays eggs, or a cow gives birth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sign with example, plus 1 mark for explaining growth as getting bigger.

34. (5 marks)
   Answer: Water when dry, weed, do not trample, plant trees, do not pick flowers, put waste in bins, protect from animals (any five).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way up to 5.

35. (5 marks)
   Answer: They are full of air which is matter. Air takes up space. For example the upside-down cup pushed into water stays dry inside or a balloon swells with air.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for air inside, 1 mark for air is matter, 1 mark for an activity, 1 mark for the observation, 1 mark for the conclusion.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Growing towards light, roots growing down, touch-me-not folding leaves, flowers opening in the day.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: Vertebrates: goat and tilapia, have a backbone. Invertebrates: ant and snail, have no backbone.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two vertebrates, 1 mark for feature, 1 mark for two invertebrates, 1 mark for feature.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Heat from the sun makes the water evaporate. It changes to vapour and goes into the air so the clothes become dry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sun heat, 1 mark for evaporation, 1 mark for the result.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Push dry tissue into the bottom of the cup. Turn the cup upside down and push it straight down into water. Lift it out. The tissue is dry because air took up the space in the cup and kept the water out.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for set up, 1 mark for pushing into water, 1 mark for dry tissue, 1 mark for conclusion.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: Heat from fire, gas or electricity cooks food making it soft and safer. Heat from fire or clothes keeps the body warm and chicks warm.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four points.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wear gloves and closed shoes, use a rake or shovel, do not touch sharp objects, wash hands afterwards, do not burn waste.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: The body loses water quickly and the person becomes weak, especially young children. They should drink clean water and ORS, rest, see a health worker and keep clean.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for dangers, 3 marks for actions.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Each grain of sand is a small solid with its own shape. The grains are piled together and pour as a pile.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for grains being solids, 1 mark for grains having shape, 1 mark for conclusion.
